summary: Cascade fallback to quantized variants caused high tail latency for NimbleDocs dedicated pool — customer escalation
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-10 between 11:42-12:05 UTC NimbleDocs observed high 95/99th percentile generation latency (spikes from ~200ms to up to 3.8s) and intermittent streaming disconnects for chat endpoints. Customer reported increased user-facing errors and slow responses during a high-traffic campaign window. Customer traffic is on a Dedicated pool in us-west and eu-central with routing policy that prefers full-precision variants and falls back to quantized variants when capacity-constrained.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat UX degraded; several sessions timed out and streaming sessions disconnected (estimated 8% of active sessions during window).
- Billing and SLA risk for a paying Dedicated customer.
- Customer opened an escalation to Support and threatened reduced traffic to Redwood if not remediated.

Timeline (condensed):
- 11:40 UTC: NimbleDocs spike begins (campaign). Autoscaler begins evicting/creating pods to match load.
- 11:42 UTC: Observability shows routing layer started failing to bind requests to primary FP instances for short windows and routed ~22% of traffic to quantized variants.
- 11:45 UTC: Latency 95/99p increases recorded in prod-us-west and eu-central; streaming disconnects spike.
- 11:50 UTC: Support engaged SRE; immediate mitigation actions started (traffic steering and rollbacks).
- 12:03 UTC: Temporary routing policy rollback completed; traffic returned to FP variants and tails normalized by 12:05 UTC.

Investigation notes / Observations:
- Autoscaler churn: we saw frequent node-level evictions within the Dedicated pool triggered by a transient GPU driver patch (we had pushed a scheduled driver update to a subset of hosts in us-west earlier in the day). This produced short windows where advertised FP capacity dropped.
- Routing decision code (router) has a fallback threshold that will flip traffic to quantized variants if observed FP availability < 85% for 30s. Due to autoscaler churn, the router flipped and then stayed in fallback for additional cycles because the health check windowed metric used for promotion back to FP had a 3-minute smoothing window.
- Quantized runtime exhibited higher tail latency under the specific prompt length distribution of NimbleDocs (long chat histories + streaming tokens), because KV cache handling in the 8-bit path interacted poorly with streaming prefetch heuristics.
- Observed a small memory leak in the quantized path that caused a few instances to hit an OOM threshold and restart during the window, which extended the fallback period.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate traffic pattern: high concurrency with long chat histories (median context 2.5k tokens, tail 6k).
2) Force FP pool availability to drop below 85% for ~1 minute via controlled instance draining.
3) Observe router flip to quantized variants and measure 95/99p latencies for streaming endpoints.

Logs & links:
- Kibana: logs/session-errors?#time=2026-03-10T11:40:00Z-2026-03-10T12:10:00Z
- Grafana: dashboard/redwood/dedicated-pool/us-west?from=2026-03-10T11:30Z&to=2026-03-10T12:10Z
- Router traces: https://traces.redwood.com/trace/SUP-53122

Workaround applied:
- Immediate: temporarily lowered router fallback sensitivity and forced routing to FP variants for NimbleDocs Dedicated pool. This required a config toggle to bypass the 3-minute re-promotion smoothing window.
- Short-term: pinned NimbleDocs to a committed subset of warm FP instances while SRE investigated the quantized runtime leak.

Resolution summary:
- Reverted the routing re-promotion smoothing window to allow faster switchback to FP when observed availability recovered.
- Rolled back the morning GPU driver patch from the small subset of hosts that were experiencing instability; autoscaler churn stopped.
- Deployed a fix to the quantized runtime that reduces KV cache prefetch contention and prevents the observed OOM (~patch 1892).
- Post-fix monitoring showed 99p latency return to baseline within 20 minutes of full rollback.

Customer communication:
- Support sent interim updates at 11:55 UTC and 12:10 UTC while mitigation steps were underway.
- Final post-incident summary and root-cause explanation was shared with NimbleDocs on 2026-03-13. Customer accepted remediation and requested follow-ups (below).

resolution_notes: Mitigations: rolled back driver patch on affected hosts, reverted router re-promotion smoothing, deployed quantized runtime fix (PR 1892). No further customer impact observed after rollbacks. NimbleDocs confirmed user experience recovered. SLA credits evaluated and offered per policy; customer accepted credit and will maintain Dedicated contract.
investigation_notes: Primary contributor was operational churn (driver patch evictions) that temporarily reduced FP capacity. Router fallback logic and re-promotion smoothing amplified impact by keeping traffic on quantized variants longer than necessary. Secondary contributor was a quantized runtime memory leak that extended instance churn. Root cause spans infra (driver rollout), router policy tuning, and quantized runtime robustness.
post_incident_action_items: Action-1: Update runbook to include immediate toggle for router re-promotion smoothing (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-20)
Action-2: Add canary gate for GPU driver rollouts to Dedicated pools to prevent parallel evictions (owner: Infra, due: 2026-04-01)
Action-3: Improve quantized path e2e tests with long-history streaming scenarios (owner: Runtime Team, due: 2026-03-28)
Action-4: Create metric alert for rapid FP availability drops (>10% drop in 60s) tied to automated paging (owner: Observability, due: 2026-03-22)
Action-5: Schedule a dedicated-customer review with NimbleDocs to discuss workload characterization and recommended model/quant profiles (owner: Customer Success, due: 2026-03-25)
Action-6: Postmortem document published and shared with CS & Engineering (link in related_confluence_pages).
